newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to spend PLN 400 mln to fix flooded roads.
newsitem.headline: Poland to spend PLN 400 mln to fix flooded roads.

text.p: Poland will spend about 400 million zlotys in 1997 to repair roads and railways damaged by July's catastrophic floods, Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said on Thursday.
Liberadzki said the sum, with half to be spent on raods and half on railways, will cover just basic repairs and more would have to be spent on full reconstruction.
"About 200 million zlotys is the cost of making all roads usable," he told a news conference.
He added that by the year 2001 Poland would spend about two billion zlotys on repairing and then upgrading flood-hit railways to Euroepan Union's standards, as envisaged by international agreements.
The transport ministry also said in a statment that the floods affected 2,000 km of railways, more than 3,000 km of roads, many bridges and other transport facilities.
